candidate.title: Quartz-Seq
candidate.scope: The original single-cell Quartz-Seq whole-transcript-amplification architecture in the assigned Illumina poster row: poly(A)-primed reverse transcription, RT-primer digestion, cDNA poly(A) tailing, tagging-primer second-strand synthesis, PCR-stage primer addition, and suppression PCR to amplified cDNA. The card title and row define one target. The candidate catalogue page was verified by its Quartz-Seq heading and matching scheme. Adjacent MARS-Seq, DP-Seq, barcode workflows and chemical structures are outside this row. Quartz-Chip, modified cell-mass applications, related methods and downstream LIMprep are not alternative targets here. The endpoint is WTA cDNA rather than a completed Illumina sequencing library. Primary-paper-supported interpretation of the poster’s LNA-primer label is explicit in c1.

operations.label: Enrich with suppres-sion PCR
operations.description: Amplifies the cDNA preparation through its WTA primer handles while suppressing enrichment of short DNA fragments, including primer-derived byproducts, to yield the final depicted cDNA.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper explains that complementary terminal sequences in short DNA can self-anneal into a pan-like structure, obstructing PCR-primer binding. Suppression depends on the terminal sequences and fragment structure.
operations.information_effect: Increases the quantity of transcript-derived DNA for sequencing. The readout carrier is amplified cDNA, so downstream sequences report represented RNA expression rather than direct counts of individual input RNA molecules. PCR representation can be biased; no UMI or cell-barcode assignment is depicted.

method_scopes.rationale: All six local operation captions belong to the single Quartz-Seq row. They describe the single-cell WTA component of the original Sasagawa et al. implementation; o2 combines the captioned RT and primer-digestion actions, while o5 preserves the drawn reagent-addition boundary. The primary WTA protocol has five main biochemical steps because primer addition is part of the PCR step. There is one continuous sample route with no depicted split, pooling or alternative workflow. The single-cell association is maintained by the sample/tube, with no cell barcode or UMI depicted. The T7 segment does not create an RNA-amplification branch. Readout interpretation: subsequent sequencing of DNA libraries derived from this cDNA supports RNA-expression profiling and comparisons between cells, subject to amplification and representation bias. Paper-supported fragmentation/adaptor ligation explains the sequencing interface but is not expanded into unshown graph operations.
